comments.author: femmi_ne
comments.body_html:
After more testing, I think the issue is not really caused by video quality itself or insufficient GPU power.

It seems more like the animated texture system breaks once the internally generated texture/render target exceeds Unity’s limits.

What I observed:

  • Higher resolution/high FPS videos cause severe stuttering.
  • Lowering the video from 4K to 1440p removed the stutter almost completely.
  • HOWEVER, the animated texture/video playback still broke after entering raid.

So lowering the source quality reduced the severity, but did not actually fix the underlying issue.

The logs still show:

  • oversized generated texture dimensions (5200x780, 4280x1080)
  • RenderTexture creation failures
  • Graphics.Blit pass failures afterward

This makes me think: the problem is not “the GPU cannot handle the video”. Specially when i am using RTX 4090.

Instead, it looks like:

  • the runtime-generated animated texture/atlas/render target exceeds Unity limits, at this case 4096x4096
  • and once that happens, the rendering pipeline partially fails.

Reducing the video quality simply reduces how badly the system breaks.

That would explain why:

  • extremely large videos produce heavy stutter,
  • while smaller ones only cause playback failure,
  • but both still trigger the same internal texture/render issues.

So I think the root issue is likely:

  • missing texture size clamping,
  • atlas/frame-strip generation exceeding safe dimensions,
  • or missing fallback handling after RenderTexture creation fails.

Especially because nearby Fika clients also experience the stutter when looking at the player, which suggests the generated runtime textures/materials are being rebuilt or loaded on all clients.

Hope i provide enough info to help. Cause i am unable to do anything at this point :( Pictures dont break anything cause its one frame but videos (i was specially looking into) breaks randomly..anytime in raid or stash.

comments.body_html:
Body armors, rigs, backpacks, arm bands, some helmets and facemasks have two completely different models: first is static mesh used for loose loot, shown inside stat card and inventory icon, second is skeletal mesh weared on character which follows bones and bends with animations. Apply Paint editor uses static model, so if you put stickers on it, they will end up in completely different place once you equip item on character (sometimes 1000 meters underground), and since stickers dont stick to character bones, they will weirdly shift with any character movement.
